hints: The tail event $X > 5$ means that the first 5 trials are all failures, requiring no success factor.

walkthrough.text:
Identify that the event $X > 5$ corresponds to the first 5 trials all resulting in failure:
$$P(X > 5) = q^5 = (1 - p)^5$$
$$\text{where } p = 0.20, \quad q = 0.80$$

Evaluate the power:
$$P(X > 5) = (0.80)^5 = 0.32768$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
A tail probability uses only failure powers:
$$P(X > 5) = 0.80^5$$

hints: The cumulative probability $P(X \le 4)$ is the complement of all 4 trials failing: $1 - q^4$.
Compute $1 - (0.85)^4 = 1 - 0.522006 = 0.4780$ to 4 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Use the complement rule where success occurring within 4 trials is the opposite of 4 consecutive failures:
$$P(X \le 4) = 1 - P(X > 4) = 1 - q^4$$
$$\text{where } q = 1 - 0.15 = 0.85$$

Compute the numerical value:
$$P(X \le 4) = 1 - (0.85)^4 = 1 - 0.52200625 = 0.47799375 \dots \approx 0.4780 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Subtract the chance of 4 straight failures from 1:
$$P(X \le 4) = 1 - 0.85^4$$

hints: Because $X$ takes integer values, the event $X \ge 4$ means that the first success occurs on roll 4 or later, so rolls 1, 2, and 3 must all fail.

walkthrough.text:
Translate the weak inequality $X \ge 4$ into a strict tail inequality:
$$X \ge 4 \iff X > 3 \iff \text{the first 3 rolls fail}$$

Apply the tail formula with $q = 1 - 1/6 = 5/6$:
$$P(X \ge 4) = q^3 = \left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^3 = \frac{125}{216}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
At least 4 rolls means the first 3 rolls were not 6:
$$P(X \ge 4) = \left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^3$$

walkthrough.text:
Express the closed interval as the difference of two cumulative probabilities:
$$P(3 \le X \le 6) = P(X \le 6) - P(X \le 2) = (1 - q^6) - (1 - q^2) = q^2 - q^6$$
$$\text{where } q = 1 - 0.30 = 0.70$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Subtract the probability of finishing in 2 or fewer trials from finishing in 6 or fewer:
$$P(3 \le X \le 6) = 0.70^2 - 0.70^6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up difference of cumulative terms or tails: $P(X \le 6) - P(X \le 2) = (1 - 0.70^6) - (1 - 0.70^2) = 0.70^2 - 0.70^6$.

hints: The probability of at least one success in $n$ trials is $1 - (1 - 0.25)^n = 1 - (0.75)^n$.
Solve $1 - (0.75)^n > 0.90 \implies (0.75)^n < 0.10 \implies n > \ln(0.10) / \ln(0.75) \approx 8.004$, so the least integer is $n = 9$.

walkthrough.text:
Formulate the inequality using the complement of zero successes in $n$ trials:
$$P(\text{at least one success}) = 1 - (0.75)^n > 0.90 \implies (0.75)^n < 0.10$$

Apply logarithms, noting that $\ln(0.75) < 0$ reverses the inequality direction:
$$n \ln(0.75) < \ln(0.10) \implies n > \frac{\ln(0.10)}{\ln(0.75)} = \frac{-2.302585}{-0.287682} \approx 8.0039 \implies n = 9$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Solve with logarithms and choose the next whole number:
$$n > \frac{\ln(0.10)}{\ln(0.75)} \approx 8.004 \implies n = 9$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up inequality $1 - 0.75^n > 0.90 \implies 0.75^n < 0.10$ and takes logarithms to find $n > \frac{\ln(0.10)}{\ln(0.75)} \approx 8.004$.

hints: For a geometric distribution, $P(X > 3) = q^3$. Solve $q^3 = 0.216$ to find $q = 0.60$ and $p = 0.40$.

walkthrough.text:
Use the tail probability formula to determine the failure parameter $q$:
$$P(X > 3) = q^3 = 0.216 \implies q = \sqrt[3]{0.216} = 0.60 \implies p = 1 - 0.60 = 0.40$$

Evaluate $P(X \le 2)$ using the cumulative formula:
$$P(X \le 2) = 1 - q^2 = 1 - (0.60)^2 = 1 - 0.36 = 0.64$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Take the cube root of the tail probability:
$$q^3 = 0.216 \implies q = 0.60, \quad p = 0.40$$

Find the cumulative probability for 2 trials:
$$P(X \le 2) = 1 - 0.60^2 = 0.64$$

hints: Find the proportion of mint sweets: $p = 3 / (3 + 4 + 5) = 3/12 = 1/4$, so $q = 3/4$.
The tail probability $P(X > 6)$ requires 6 consecutive non-mint sweets: $(3/4)^6 = 729 / 4096 \approx 0.1780$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the single-trial probabilities from the given ratio:
$$\text{Total parts } = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 \implies p = \frac{3}{12} = \frac{1}{4}, \quad q = 1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$$

Calculate $P(X > 6)$ using the tail formula:
$$P(X > 6) = q^6 = \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^6 = \frac{729}{4096} \approx 0.1780 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find $p$ and $q$ from the ratio:
$$p = \frac{3}{12} = 0.25, \quad q = 0.75$$

Six non-mint sweets must be dispensed:
$$P(X > 6) = 0.75^6 = \frac{729}{4096} \approx 0.1780$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates success probability $p = \frac{3}{3+4+5} = \frac{3}{12} = \frac{1}{4}$ and failure probability $q = \frac{3}{4} = 0.75$.

hints: No more than 4 sweets dispensed means $X \le 4$, which is calculated as $1 - q^4$.

walkthrough.text:
Express no more than 4 sweets as a cumulative probability using the complement:
$$P(X \le 4) = 1 - P(X > 4) = 1 - q^4 = 1 - \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^4$$

Evaluate the fraction:
$$P(X \le 4) = 1 - \frac{81}{256} = \frac{256 - 81}{256} = \frac{175}{256} \approx 0.6836 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Subtract the probability of 4 failures from 1:
$$P(X \le 4) = 1 - \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^4$$

hints: The event that the first success is among the first 3 customers is $P(X \le 3) = 1 - (0.68)^3$.

walkthrough.text:
Formulate the cumulative probability for $X \le 3$ with $p = 0.32$ and $q = 0.68$:
$$P(X \le 3) = 1 - q^3 = 1 - (0.68)^3$$

$$P(X \le 3) = 1 - 0.314432 = 0.685568$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the complement of 3 non-online shoppers:
$$P(X \le 3) = 1 - 0.68^3$$

hints: Set up the threshold inequality: $1 - (0.68)^n > 0.96 \implies (0.68)^n < 0.04$.
Take logarithms: $n > \ln(0.04) / \ln(0.68) \approx 8.346$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the probability of at least one success exceeding $0.96$:
$$1 - (0.68)^n > 0.96 \implies (0.68)^n < 0.04$$

Take natural logarithms, reversing the inequality because $\ln(0.68) < 0$:
$$n \ln(0.68) < \ln(0.04) \implies n > \frac{\ln(0.04)}{\ln(0.68)} = \frac{-3.218876}{-0.385662} \approx 8.3464$$

Confirm the least integer with neighbor checks:
$$\text{For } n = 8: \quad 1 - (0.68)^8 \approx 0.9543 < 0.96$$
$$\text{For } n = 9: \quad 1 - (0.68)^9 \approx 0.9689 > 0.96 \implies n = 9$$

ai_rubric.observable: States least integer $n = 9$ with neighbor checks $1 - 0.68^8 \approx 0.9543 < 0.96$ and $1 - 0.68^9 \approx 0.9689 > 0.96$.

hints: The outcomes $\{1, 6\}$ give success probability $p = 2/6 = 1/3$ and $q = 2/3$.
The interval $3 \le X \le 6$ corresponds to $P(X \le 6) - P(X \le 2) = q^2 - q^6$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the parameters for obtaining a 1 or a 6 on a fair die:
$$p = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}, \quad q = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$$

Express the interval probability as the difference between two tail powers:
$$P(3 \le X \le 6) = P(X > 2) - P(X > 6) = q^2 - q^6 = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^6$$
$$= \frac{4}{9} - \frac{64}{729} = \frac{324 - 64}{729} = \frac{260}{729} \approx 0.3567 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Subtract the two tail boundaries:
$$P(3 \le X \le 6) = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^6 = \frac{260}{729}$$

hints: Express the condition as $1 - (2/3)^n > 0.995 \implies (2/3)^n < 0.005$.
Solve using natural logarithms: $n > \ln(0.005) / \ln(2/3) \approx 13.067$.
Verify that $n = 13$ fails to meet the threshold and $n = 14$ is the least integer.

walkthrough.text:
Formulate the target threshold condition:
$$P(\ge 1 \text{ success}) = 1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^n > 0.995 \implies \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^n < 0.005$$

Solve the inequality using logarithms, noting that $\ln(2/3) < 0$:
$$n \ln\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) < \ln(0.005) \implies n > \frac{\ln(0.005)}{\ln(2/3)} = \frac{-5.298317}{-0.405465} \approx 13.0673$$

Conduct neighbor checks:
$$\text{For } n = 13: \quad 1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{13} \approx 0.99486 < 0.995$$
$$\text{For } n = 14: \quad 1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{14} \approx 0.99657 > 0.995 \implies n = 14$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Conclude that 14 is the first integer passing the test:
$$n = 14$$

ai_rubric.observable: States least integer $n = 14$ with neighbor check $1 - (2/3)^{13} \approx 0.9949 < 0.995$ and $1 - (2/3)^{14} \approx 0.9966 > 0.995$.

hints: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{Geo}(0.06)$ with failure probability $q = 0.94$.
The event $5 \le X \le 12$ can be calculated directly as $q^4 - q^{12}$.

walkthrough.text:
Define the distribution for the number of bulbs tested until the first defect:
$$X \sim \text{Geo}(p = 0.06), \quad q = 1 - 0.06 = 0.94$$

Express the probability $P(5 \le X \le 12)$ as the difference between two tail events:
$$P(5 \le X \le 12) = P(X > 4) - P(X > 12) = q^4 - q^{12} = (0.94)^4 - (0.94)^{12}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the tail difference:
$$P(5 \le X \le 12) = 0.94^4 - 0.94^{12}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses interval as $P(5 \le X \le 12) = q^4 - q^{12} = 0.94^4 - 0.94^{12}$.

hints: The probability of at least one defect in a carton of $N$ bulbs is $1 - (0.94)^N$.
Take logarithms: $N \ge \ln(0.20) / \ln(0.94) \approx 26.011$, so the smallest integer size is $N = 27$.

walkthrough.text:
Formulate the target inequality for carton size $N$:
$$P(\ge 1 \text{ defective}) = 1 - (0.94)^N \ge 0.80 \implies (0.94)^N \le 0.20$$

Apply logarithms, noting that $\ln(0.94) < 0$ reverses the inequality:
$$N \ln(0.94) \le \ln(0.20) \implies N \ge \frac{\ln(0.20)}{\ln(0.94)} = \frac{-1.609438}{-0.061875} \approx 26.0109$$

Verify with neighbor calculations:
$$\text{For } N = 26: \quad 1 - (0.94)^{26} \approx 0.79986 < 0.80$$
$$\text{For } N = 27: \quad 1 - (0.94)^{27} \approx 0.81187 \ge 0.80 \implies N = 27$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set the carton failure rate below 0.20:
$$0.94^N \le 0.20$$

Round up to the next integer:
$$N = 27$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies smallest integer $N = 27$ with check $1 - (0.94)^{26} \approx 0.7999 < 0.80$ and $1 - (0.94)^{27} \approx 0.8119 > 0.80$.

hints: For any geometric distribution, $P(X > 4) = q^4$.

walkthrough.text:
State the algebraic expression for the tail probability $P(X > 4)$:
$$P(X > 4) = q^4 = (1 - p)^4 = 0.2401$$

Take the fourth root of both sides to find $q$:
$$q = \sqrt[4]{0.2401} = 0.70$$

Deduce the parameter $p$:
$$p = 1 - q = 1 - 0.70 = 0.30$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Equate the 4th power of failure to the given tail probability:
$$q^4 = 0.2401$$

hints: Notice that $2 \le X < 5$ includes $X = 2, 3, 4$ and excludes $5$.
Express as tail difference: $P(X > 1) - P(X > 4) = q^1 - q^4$.
Substitute $q = 0.70$ and evaluate $0.70 - 0.2401 = 0.4599$.

walkthrough.text:
Translate the half-open interval $2 \le X < 5$ into inclusive integer values:
$$2 \le X < 5 \iff X \in \{2, 3, 4\} \iff 2 \le X \le 4$$

Express the interval as a difference of tail probabilities with $q = 0.70$:
$$P(2 \le X \le 4) = P(X > 1) - P(X > 4) = q^1 - q^4$$

Compute the exact decimal value:
$$q^1 - q^4 = 0.70 - (0.70)^4 = 0.70 - 0.2401 = 0.4599$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the included whole numbers: 2, 3, and 4:
$$P(2 \le X < 5) = P(X > 1) - P(X > 4)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Translates half-open interval $2 \le X < 5$ into discrete values $X \in \{2, 3, 4\}$ or $P(X \le 4) - P(X \le 1) = q^1 - q^4$.

hints: Recall that for a geometric distribution, the tail probability of requiring more than $r$ trials is $P(X > r) = (1 - p)^r = q^r$.
The tail event $X > 5$ represents 5 consecutive misses, with no final success probability included.
Compute $(0.78)^5 = 0.288717 \dots$ and round to 4 significant figures: $0.2887$.

walkthrough.text:
State the geometric model for the archer:
$$X \sim \text{Geo}(p = 0.22), \quad q = 1 - 0.22 = 0.78$$

Evaluate the tail probability of needing more than 5 shots:
$$P(X > 5) = q^5 = (0.78)^5 = 0.28871744 \dots \approx 0.2887 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

hints: The probability of at least one hit in $n$ shots is $1 - (0.78)^n$.
Solve with logarithms: $n > \ln(0.05) / \ln(0.78) \approx 12.057$.
Choose the least integer above the boundary, which is $n = 13$.

walkthrough.text:
Formulate the threshold inequality for the archer:
$$1 - (0.78)^n > 0.95 \implies (0.78)^n < 0.05$$

Apply natural logarithms, reversing the inequality because $\ln(0.78) < 0$:
$$n \ln(0.78) < \ln(0.05) \implies n > \frac{\ln(0.05)}{\ln(0.78)} = \frac{-2.995732}{-0.248461} \approx 12.0571$$

Verify with neighbor checks:
$$\text{For } n = 12: \quad 1 - (0.78)^{12} \approx 0.94929 < 0.95$$
$$\text{For } n = 13: \quad 1 - (0.78)^{13} \approx 0.96044 > 0.95 \implies n = 13$$

ai_rubric.observable: States least integer $n = 13$ with checks $1 - 0.78^{12} \approx 0.9493 < 0.95$ and $1 - 0.78^{13} \approx 0.9604 > 0.95$.

hints: In one round of 4 shots, the probability that all 4 archers miss is $(0.78)^4 = 0.370151$.
The probability of needing at most 2 rounds is $1 - (q_{\text{round}})^2 = 1 - (0.78^4)^2 = 1 - (0.78)^8$.
Round to 3 significant figures: $0.863$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability that none of the 4 archers hit the target in a single round:
$$q_{\text{round}} = (1 - 0.22)^4 = (0.78)^4 = 0.37015056$$
$$p_{\text{round}} = 1 - q_{\text{round}} = 1 - 0.37015056 = 0.62984944$$

Define $Y \sim \text{Geo}(p_{\text{round}})$ and express $P(Y \le 2)$ using the cumulative formula:
$$P(Y \le 2) = 1 - (q_{\text{round}})^2 = 1 - \left((0.78)^4\right)^2 = 1 - (0.78)^8$$

Compute the numerical value to 3 significant figures:
$$P(Y \le 2) = 1 - (0.78)^8 = 1 - 0.13701144 = 0.86298856 \dots \approx 0.863 \text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the chance of no hit across all 4 archers in round 1:
$$q_{\text{round}} = 0.78^4 = 0.3702$$

Both rounds must completely fail for $Y > 2$:
$$P(Y \le 2) = 1 - (0.78^4)^2 = 1 - 0.78^8$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds probability that no archer hits target in one round: $q_{\text{round}} = (0.78)^4 = 0.370151$.

hints: The number of components tested follows $X \sim \text{Geo}(0.12)$ with non-failure probability $q = 0.88$.
The interval $4 \le X \le 10$ is calculated as $P(X > 3) - P(X > 10) = q^3 - q^{10}$.
Round to 4 significant figures: $0.4030$.

walkthrough.text:
Define the distribution for the test sequence:
$$X \sim \text{Geo}(p = 0.12), \quad q = 1 - 0.12 = 0.88$$

Formulate the interval probability using tail powers:
$$P(4 \le X \le 10) = P(X > 3) - P(X > 10) = q^3 - q^{10} = (0.88)^3 - (0.88)^{10}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Subtract the two tail limits:
$$P(4 \le X \le 10) = 0.88^3 - 0.88^{10}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up interval formula $P(4 \le X \le 10) = q^3 - q^{10} = 0.88^3 - 0.88^{10}$.

hints: The probability of at least one failure in a batch of $k$ items is $1 - (0.88)^k$.
Take logarithms: $k > \ln(0.25) / \ln(0.88) \approx 10.845$.
State the least integer value: $k = 11$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the threshold inequality for batch size $k$:
$$P(\ge 1 \text{ failure}) = 1 - (0.88)^k > 0.75 \implies (0.88)^k < 0.25$$

Solve with natural logarithms, reversing the inequality because $\ln(0.88) < 0$:
$$k \ln(0.88) < \ln(0.25) \implies k > \frac{\ln(0.25)}{\ln(0.88)} = \frac{-1.386294}{-0.127833} \approx 10.8445$$

Perform neighbor checks:
$$\text{For } k = 10: \quad 1 - (0.88)^{10} \approx 0.7215 < 0.75$$
$$\text{For } k = 11: \quad 1 - (0.88)^{11} \approx 0.7549 > 0.75 \implies k = 11$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set the batch survival rate below 0.25:
$$0.88^k < 0.25$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies least integer $k = 11$ with checks $1 - 0.88^{10} \approx 0.7215 < 0.75$ and $1 - 0.88^{11} \approx 0.7549 > 0.75$.

hints: Use the batch probability from part (b): $q_{\text{batch}} = 1 - (0.88)^{11} = 0.754919$.
Define the outer model for counting batches: $W \sim B(5, q_{\text{batch}})$.
Evaluate $P(W = 4) = 5(q_{\text{batch}})^4(1 - q_{\text{batch}})$.
Compute the numerical value and round to 3 significant figures: $0.398$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the success probability for an entire 11-component batch:
$$q_{\text{batch}} = 1 - (0.88)^{11} = 1 - 0.24508086 = 0.75491914$$
$$1 - q_{\text{batch}} = (0.88)^{11} = 0.24508086$$

Define the outer binomial model where one trial is a full batch of 11 components:
$$W \sim B(n = 5, p = 0.75491914)$$
$$P(W = 4) = \binom{5}{4} p^4 (1 - p)^1 = 5 p^4 (1 - p)$$

Evaluate the arithmetic:
$$P(W = 4) = 5 \times (0.75491914)^4 \times 0.24508086 = 5 \times 0.32478791 \times 0.24508086 = 0.39799824 \dots \approx 0.398 \text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the success rate for one batch of 11 items:
$$p = 1 - 0.88^{11} = 0.7549$$

Set up the binomial formula for 4 successes in 5 batches:
$$P(W = 4) = 5(0.7549)^4(0.2451)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies batch failure probability $q_{\text{batch}} = 1 - (0.88)^{11} = 1 - 0.245081 = 0.754919$ and outer binomial model $W \sim B(5, q_{\text{batch}})$.
